headline: Financial Services strength lifts margins, guidance raised
summary_short: Cognizant reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5,481M, up 4.5% y/y, as Financial Services grew 12.0% y/y; adjusted operating margin expanded 40bp to 16.0% and diluted EPS rose 3.8% y/y to $1.36, even as net income slipped 1.4% y/y to $636M on a higher tax provision.
summary_long: Revenue reached $5,481M (+4.5% y/y, +4.1% CC), led by a second straight quarter of double-digit Financial Services growth (+12.0% y/y) plus modest lifts from recent acquisitions and third-party product sales. Adjusted operating margin expanded 40bp y/y to 16.0%; GAAP margin gained 30bp to 15.9% as $84M of Project Leap charges were nearly offset by an $81M one-time India defined-contribution benefit. Net income of $636M fell 1.4% y/y on a higher tax provision, though diluted EPS still rose 3.8% to $1.36 as $1.15B of buybacks cut share count. Cash fell to $1,038M (-42.2% y/y) after the $634M Astreya deal. Cognizant raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $5.70-$5.82; margin guidance is unchanged at 16.0%-16.2%.

drivers.explanation: Financial Services grew 12.0% y/y (11.7% CC) for a second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, the company's largest segment; recent acquisitions added ~100bp and third-party product sales ~170bp to total revenue growth.

Adjusted operating margin rose 40bp y/y on execution discipline; GAAP margin gained only 30bp because an $84M Project Leap restructuring charge was nearly offset by an $81M one-time India defined-contribution-obligation benefit booked to SG&A.

Pre-tax income rose y/y ($875M vs $842M) but the tax provision increased more ($231M vs $197M) and equity-method investments swung to an $8M loss from breakeven, producing a small net-income decline despite higher operating income.
EPS outgrew net income because diluted shares fell to 466M from 492M y/y, reflecting $1.15B of second-quarter buybacks (22.5M shares) that shrank the denominator faster than income declined.

Management credits AI-driven client demand and Financial Services scale for the growth, and prioritized capital toward $1.15B of buybacks and the $634M Astreya acquisition to expand AI-services delivery capacity.
